Mechanism family: conflict-graph-neighborhood local search
Replacement scope: Re
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: conflict-graph-neighborhood local search
Replacement scope: Replace the randomized-restart phase of `get_best_schedule` (the `while time.time() > deadline` loop calling `build`) with a first-improvement local search over complete permutations. Keep the initial pure-greedy baseline phase as the starting solution generator.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent only constructs schedules forward greedily and never revisits a completed schedule; many near-optimal orderings differ from a greedy one by a few adjacent positions. Local search exposes a new degree of freedom (repositioning already-placed transactions) that no amount of additional greedy restarts can reach.
Compute budget: Each swap/insertion evaluation is one `get_opt_seq_cost` call (~ms). Budget: continue until per-workload deadline (~100s), evaluating at most a few thousand moves per pass; no new optimizer starts beyond the greedy baseline already present. Evaluation-time effect: same wall-clock envelope as incumbent.
Plan: Start from the best greedy schedule. Repeatedly scan all adjacent-pair swaps (positions i, i+1) and single-transaction reinsertions (remove txn at position i, insert at position j, |i-j|≤3). Accept the first improving move (first-improvement) or the best move per pass if scans are cheap; recompute cost only for the modified sequence via `get_opt_seq_cost(seq)`. When no improving move exists, perturb: apply 3 random swaps and continue (basic iterated local search, still within the same mechanism family of neighborhood moves). Keep a global best; return it before deadline. Hard validity: every candidate is a full permutation of `range(n)` (swaps/reinsertions preserve permutation), so the caller's `get_opt_seq_cost` always receives a valid complete schedule; the incumbent greedy result is retained as fallback if local search never improves.
Expected-gain check: The new degree of freedom — repositioning already-placed transactions via swaps/reinsertions — is unreachable by the incumbent's forward-only greedy construction; falsifiable threshold: total makespan strictly below the incumbent's measured 291 on the same evaluator, i.e., combined_score > 3424.66.

strategies.title: Mechanism family: layered topological construction over the read/write conflict
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: layered topological construction over the read/write conflict graph
Replacement scope: Replace the entire construction mechanism inside `get_best_schedule` (both the greedy baseline and the `build` restarts) with a dependency-layered constructor, then spend remaining budget on local swaps.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent picks transactions one at a time by immediate incremental cost, which myopically serializes conflicting transactions and misses the global structure: transactions with no conflicts between them can be ordered freely at zero marginal delay. A layer-based construction explicitly exploits conflict-free parallelism, a structural degree of freedom the greedy scan cannot see.
Compute budget: One layered construction per candidate tie-breaking order (O(n + edges) per pass, no `get_opt_seq_cost` calls during construction). Budget: up to ~200 randomized layered constructions (~seconds total), then the remaining ~90s per workload for swap local search on the best layer schedule. Evaluation-time effect: unchanged envelope.
Plan: Build a directed conflict graph among transactions: edge u→v if u and v touch a common key and at least one operation is a write (derive from workload operations; if the workload object exposes item→txn maps use those, otherwise parse the txn operation lists once and cache). Compute a layering: layer 0 = transactions with no unresolved predecessors; repeatedly place a transaction in the next layer once all its predecessors are in earlier layers (this is a topological layering of the conflict DAG — any within-layer order is conflict-free). Within each layer, order transactions by a randomized tie-break weighted by incremental true cost: for small layers evaluate all orderings' incremental cost via `get_opt_seq_cost` on the prefix; for large layers use the greedy incremental pick. Concatenate layers into a full permutation. Randomize tie-breaks across restarts, keep the best full schedule, then refine with adjacent-swap local search until deadline. Hard validity: output is always a concatenation of all n transactions exactly once (each transaction enters exactly one layer), so the permutation constraint is preserved by construction; keep the identity permutation as initial fallback.
Expected-gain check: The new degree of freedom is conflict-layer parallelism — reordering within conflict-free layers changes makespan without changing any conflict dependency, a reordering subspace the incumbent's sequential greedy never systematically explores; falsifiable threshold: total makespan < 291 (combined_score > 3424.66) on the same evaluator.

strategies.title:
Mechanism family: beam-search partial-schedule expansion
Replacement scope: Repl
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: beam-search partial-schedule expansion
Replacement scope: Replace the greedy construction and randomized restarts in `get_best_schedule` with a breadth-limited beam search over partial permutations, plus a short swap-refinement tail.
Gain mechanism: Greedy is a beam of width 1 and commits irrevocably to one prefix; randomized restarts sample prefixes independently and never share partial progress. Beam search keeps k diverse partial prefixes alive and prunes only after comparing true costs at equal depth, correcting the incumbent's observed bottleneck (irreversible myopic prefix commitment) with a genuinely different search topology.
Compute budget: Beam width k=8–16, expanding each partial state with a sampled candidate set of ~n/4 next transactions; total `get_opt_seq_cost` calls bounded by k × (n/4) × n per pass ≈ tens of thousands (feasible in ~60–80s per workload at the observed ms-scale cost). One beam pass per workload, then remaining time for swap local search on the beam's best complete schedule. Evaluation-time effect: within the same ~100s per-workload envelope; a complete valid permutation is produced immediately (identity fallback) before any search begins.
Plan: State = (partial sequence, its true cost). Initialize k states with different single starting transactions. At each depth, for each state, sample ~n/4 unplaced transactions, evaluate `get_opt_seq_cost(partial + [t])`, collect all (state, t, cost) successors, and keep the k cheapest as the next beam (optionally enforce diversity by capping successors sharing the same prefix). When the beam empties of unplaced transactions, the cheapest complete sequence is the result. Cache prefix costs to avoid recomputation where the simulator allows repeated calls cheaply. Finish with adjacent-swap first-improvement until the deadline. Hard validity: every beam state is a partial permutation extended by distinct unplaced transactions, so any completed state is a full permutation of `range(n)`; the function always returns the best complete permutation found plus the identity fallback if the beam fails early.
Expected-gain check: The new degree of freedom is maintaining k competing partial prefixes with true-cost pruning at equal depth — the incumbent's width-1 greedy and independent restarts cannot retain and compare partial prefixes; falsifiable threshold: total makespan < 291 (combined_score > 3424.66) on the same evaluator.

strategies.title: [conflict-key-clustering construction] greedy nearest-conflict insertion with ke
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: conflict-key-clustering constructive heuristic
Replacement scope: Replace the beam-search construction phase inside `get_best_schedule` (the block from `starts = list(range(min(beam_k, n)))` through the beam loop and `completions` harvesting); keep the cached `seq_cost`, the identity fallback, and the ILS refinement tail unchanged.
Compute budget: ~10s per workload for construction (n greedy restarts, each O(n²) with cheap incremental conflict-affinity scoring, no simulator calls inside the greedy loop), leaving ~45s for the existing ILS tail within a 55s per-workload deadline.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent beam expands prefixes by sampled true-cost evaluation, which is myopic about *why* a prefix is cheap: transactions sharing write keys should be adjacent to avoid repeated conflict-delay re-arming between distant same-key writers. New degree of freedom: build permutations by greedy insertion ordered by conflict-graph affinity — precompute per-transaction read/write key sets, define affinity(i,j) = |keys(i) ∩ keys(j)| weighted by writes; construct each restart by starting from the transaction with highest total conflict degree, then repeatedly appending the unplaced transaction maximizing affinity to the last k placed transactions (ties broken by conflict degree), with randomized tie-breaking per restart. Feed the best few constructed permutations (evaluated with the true oracle) as seeds into the existing ILS tail alongside the identity fallback. This produces structurally different starting topologies (key-clustered orderings) that the beam's prefix-cost myopia cannot reach; the ILS then polishes them. Validity: every construction appends distinct unplaced transactions, so each seed is a complete permutation of range(n); the identity permutation remains the pre-search fallback. Expected-gain check: if key-clustered seeds let the ILS tail reach even one lower-cost local optimum than the beam seeds on any workload, total makespan drops below 254 and combined_score exceeds 3921.57 — falsifiable by direct evaluation.

strategies.title: [lexicase-tournament ILS] population-based ILS with restart selection by cost+di
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: population iterated local search with diversity-aware restart selection
Replacement scope: Replace the single-incumbent ILS tail (the block after `best_seq, best_cost = local_search(...)`, i.e., the seeds/ruin-and-recreate loop) with a small population (size 4) of schedules maintained until deadline; keep beam construction, `seq_cost` cache, and `local_search`/`one_pass` as-is.
Compute budget: Same 55s per-workload deadline; population of 4, each restart is one ruin-and-recreate + one `local_search` pass (bounded by existing `one_pass` first-improvement sweeps), so no new unbounded loops.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent ILS keeps a single current solution; when its ruin-and-recreate perturbation repeatedly reinserts segments into the same basin, all restart budget is spent on one topology. New degree of freedom: maintain 4 diverse schedules (initialized from beam completions + identity); on each restart cycle, pick the parent by lexicase-style tournament — with probability 0.5 pick the cheapest, otherwise pick the one maximally distant (Kendall-tau / position-difference) from the current best — apply the existing segment ruin-and-recreate, run `local_search`, and replace the worst-cost population member if the child improves on it. This diversifies escape directions so the search can leave basins the single-chain ILS is locked into, while the accept-only-if-better population update plus best-ever tracking guarantees the returned schedule is never worse than the incumbent's. Validity: all population members remain full permutations; final return is the best-ever permutation. Expected-gain check: the new degree of freedom is parent selection across multiple basins; if any of the added basins contains a local optimum cheaper than 254 total makespan, combined_score strictly exceeds 3921.57 — falsifiable because the population strictly dominates the single-chain ILS's reachable set.

strategies.title: [suffix-regret beam] beam search with completion-cost lookahead via suffix estim
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: lookahead-augmented beam search (suffix-regret scoring)
Replacement scope: Replace the beam-selection logic inside the beam loop of `get_best_schedule` (the successor scoring and `new_beam` selection block); keep prefix expansion, diversity cap, ILS tail, and cache.
Compute budget: 55s per-workload deadline unchanged; lookahead scores are computed from a precomputed conflict-structure table (one O(n²) pass before the beam), so per-successor cost is O(1) beyond the existing cached oracle call — no new simulator calls.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent ranks beam successors purely by prefix true cost, which systematically biases toward cheap early prefixes that strand high-conflict transactions for the end (where their conflicts cost the most). New degree of freedom: score each successor as prefix_cost + λ·regret(suffix), where regret is estimated deterministically from precomputed per-transaction conflict mass: for each unplaced transaction u, mass(u) = Σ over its keys of (number of other transactions touching that key); regret = sum of the top-m unplaced masses minus the placed ones, with λ tuned once (e.g., λ = prefix_cost / n as a scale-free default). This makes the beam prefer prefixes that keep the remaining high-conflict transactions from bunching, producing genuinely different full permutations than pure prefix-cost ranking. The true oracle still validates every completed permutation, so the returned schedule is feasible and never worse than the identity fallback. Validity: expansion still appends distinct unplaced transactions; selection only reorders candidates. Expected-gain check: the new degree of freedom is a suffix-conflict-mass lookahead the pure prefix-cost beam cannot express; if it yields any full permutation cheaper than the incumbent's beam output on a workload, total makespan < 254 and combined_score > 3921.57 — directly falsifiable by evaluation.

strategies.title: [conflict-graph layered decomposition] topological layering + within-layer ILS
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: conflict-graph layered decomposition
Replacement scope: Replace the beam-search construction phase (the whole `--- Beam search over partial permutations ---` block through the `constructed` seeds) with a layered construction; keep the ILS tail.
Compute budget: Layering is O(n²) affinity precompute (already parsed by `parse_txn`), ~2s per workload; remaining ~80s goes to per-layer ILS and the incumbent tail. Total stays within 85s/workload.
Gain mechanism: Build a conflict graph (edge = aff(i,j)>0), compute connected components; order components by descending total affinity, and inside each component greedily chain transactions by pairwise conflict affinity (nearest-conflict-neighbor path, like a TSP path on the affinity matrix). This creates a new degree of freedom the beam lacks: the beam greedily extends prefixes by true prefix cost, which is myopic about *future* conflicts; a component-path ordering provably minimizes the number of times a hot key's conflict window is re-armed across distant schedule positions. Multiple randomized restarts of the path construction (different start nodes, 2-opt path improvement on the affinity matrix) give diverse seeds to the existing ILS tail. Keep the incumbent identity/beam result as fallback; accept only if true cost improves.
Validity: every construction is a permutation of range(n); final assert preserved.
Expected-gain check: the new degree of freedom is component-level ordering + within-component conflict-path topology, which the incumbent's prefix-greedy beam cannot express (it never reorders whole conflict clusters); falsifiable threshold: total makespan strictly below the incumbent's 246 on the same three workloads.

strategies.title: [or-opt* segment-move ILS] ruin-and-recreate with or-opt(3) segment moves and si
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: or-opt segment-move ILS with annealed acceptance
Replacement scope: Replace the ILS tail (`one_pass`, `local_search`, and the final while-loop) — construction phases unchanged.
Compute budget: same 85s/workload deadline; or-opt(3) sweeps are O(n²) oracle calls per pass, unchanged order from current or-opt(1) plus segment length ≤3.
Gain mechanism: Current ILS accepts only strict improvements, so it stagnates in the incumbent's local optimum; the observed plateau (multiple attempts scoring 3921–4048) shows the accept-only-if-better guard is the bottleneck. Replace with: (a) or-opt moves over segments of length 1–3 (remove segment, reinsert at any position) instead of single-item reinsertion — a geometrically different neighborhood that reaches orderings single-item moves cannot; (b) annealed acceptance: accept a non-improving candidate with probability exp(-(c-cur_cost)/T), T decaying geometrically from 0.02·cur_cost to near zero over the budget, with restart of T on new global best. Keep the cache and true-oracle evaluation. Incumbent best_seq/best_cost always returned if nothing better found, so validity and score are never worse than current.
Expected-gain check: the new degree of freedom is multi-item segment relocation plus non-monotone escape, which the incumbent's first-improvement single-item sweep cannot realize; falsifiable threshold: makespan < 246 total across the three workloads.

strategies.title: [ant-colony pheromone construction] ACO permutation construction with conflict-a
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: ant-colony pheromone permutation construction
Replacement scope: Replace the beam-search construction and the conflict-clustering construction (both seed generators); keep seq_cost cache, ILS tail, and fallback.
Compute budget: ~25s per workload for ACO (e.g., 30 ants × ~40 iterations, each ant an O(n²) greedy walk with pheromone-weighted true-cost sampling of 5 candidates per step); remaining ~60s to ILS. Hard per-workload deadline unchanged.
Gain mechanism: Maintain an n×n pheromone matrix τ[i][j] on "transaction j placed immediately after i". Each ant builds a permutation: at each step, sample a few unplaced candidates with probability ∝ τ[last][j]^α · (1+aff(last,j))^β, evaluate the true prefix cost of extension, pick the best sampled; deposit pheromone on edges of the best ants' tours (evaporation ρ=0.1). This is a genuinely different construction mechanism: it learns *adjacency* preferences across iterations from true-cost feedback, whereas the beam's diversity cap and the clustering construction's static affinity are both memoryless. The incumbent's best mechanisms (true-cost oracle, affinity parse, ILS tail) are reused as components. Multiple ants per iteration give diverse ILS seeds; final result still guarded by the incumbent fallback.
Validity: each ant walk places each transaction exactly once (sampling only from unplaced), so every tour is a valid permutation.
Expected-gain check: the new degree of freedom is cross-iteration learned edge preference (pheromone memory) on the adjacency structure, which neither the memoryless beam nor the static affinity construction can express; falsifiable threshold: total makespan < 246 on the three workloads.

strategies.plan:

Replacement scope: Replace the beam-search construction phase (the whole `--- Beam search over partial permutations ---` block through the `constructed` seeds) with a layered construction; keep the ILS tail.
Compute budget: Layering is O(n²) affinity precompute (already parsed by `parse_txn`), ~2s per workload; remaining ~80s goes to per-layer ILS and the incumbent tail. Total stays within 85s/workload.
Gain mechanism: Build a conflict graph (edge = aff(i,j)>0), compute connected components; order components by descending total affinity, and inside each component greedily chain transactions by pairwise conflict affinity (nearest-conflict-neighbor path, like a TSP path on the affinity matrix). This creates a new degree of freedom the beam lacks: the beam greedily extends prefixes by true prefix cost, which is myopic about *future* conflicts; a component-path ordering provably minimizes the number of times a hot key's conflict window is re-armed across distant schedule positions. Multiple randomized restarts of the path construction (different start nodes, 2-opt path improvement on the affinity matrix) give diverse seeds to the existing ILS tail. Keep the incumbent identity/beam result as fallback; accept only if true cost improves.
Validity: every construction is a permutation of range(n); final assert preserved.
Expected-gain check: the new degree of freedom is component-level ordering + within-component conflict-path topology, which the incumbent's prefix-greedy beam cannot express (it never reorders whole conflict clusters); falsifiable threshold: total makespan strictly below the incumbent's 246 on the same three workloads.

strategies.title: ordered attempt [ant-colony pheromone construction] ACO permutation construction with conflict-a
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: ant-colony pheromone permutation construction
Replacement scope: Replace the beam-search construction and the conflict-clustering construction (both seed generators); keep seq_cost cache, ILS tail, and fallback.
Compute budget: ~25s per workload for ACO (e.g., 30 ants × ~40 iterations, each ant an O(n²) greedy walk with pheromone-weighted true-cost sampling of 5 candidates per step); remaining ~60s to ILS. Hard per-workload deadline unchanged.
Gain mechanism: Maintain an n×n pheromone matrix τ[i][j] on "transaction j placed immediately after i". Each ant builds a permutation: at each step, sample a few unplaced candidates with probability ∝ τ[last][j]^α · (1+aff(last,j))^β, evaluate the true prefix cost of extension, pick the best sampled; deposit pheromone on edges of the best ants' tours (evaporation ρ=0.1). This is a genuinely different construction mechanism: it learns *adjacency* preferences across iterations from true-cost feedback, whereas the beam's diversity cap and the clustering construction's static affinity are both memoryless. The incumbent's best mechanisms (true-cost oracle, affinity parse, ILS tail) are reused as components. Multiple ants per iteration give diverse ILS seeds; final result still guarded by the incumbent fallback.
Validity: each ant walk places each transaction exactly once (sampling only from unplaced), so every tour is a valid permutation.
Expected-gain check: the new degree of freedom is cross-iteration learned edge preference (pheromone memory) on the adjacency structure, which neither the memoryless beam nor the static affinity construction can express; falsifiable threshold: total makespan < 246 on the three workloads.

strategies.title: [dependency-pair order DP] conflict-order matrix + insertion-order construction
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: dependency-pair order DP (pairwise conflict-order seeding)
Replacement scope: Replace the conflict-key-clustering greedy construction block (the `chain_path`/`two_opt` layered decomposition and the positional greedy-insertion loop) inside `get_best_schedule`; keep the beam, cache, and ILS tail unchanged.
Compute budget: One O(n²) pairwise-order matrix build (~10⁴ entries for n=100, microseconds), then ≤ n greedy insertion restarts each O(n²), all inside the existing 10s construct deadline; no change to the 85s per-workload ILS budget.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent's affinity heuristic counts *shared keys*, but the true cost oracle penalizes the *order* between two conflicting transactions differently (a w→r ordering arms a different delay than r→w). The new degree of freedom is a per-pair directional cost: for each unordered pair (i, j), evaluate both orderings' true prefix cost via the oracle on 2-element sequences ([i,j] vs [j,i]) and store the cheaper direction and margin. Construction then builds seeds by repeatedly inserting the transaction whose directed conflict pressure against already-placed transactions is minimized (sum of directed pair costs into the placed set), which is a true-cost-grounded signal the incumbent's raw affinity count cannot express. Seeds feed the existing ILS tail unchanged.
Plan: (1) Parse keys as now (reuse `parse_txn`). (2) For each pair with positive affinity, compute `d(i,j) = seq_cost([i,j]) - seq_cost([j,i])` from the cached true oracle; store signed matrix D and total pair weight W. (3) Greedy: start from the transaction with max total conflict weight; iteratively append the unplaced t minimizing Σ_{p placed} D(t,p) (directed cost of t-after-p), with 3 randomized tie-break restarts. (4) Score each seed with `seq_cost`, keep near-competitive ones (existing 1.02 cutoff) as extra ILS seeds. Validity: every seed is a full permutation of range(n) built by appending distinct unplaced IDs; incumbent identity permutation and beam results remain the fallback. Expected-gain check: the incumbent cannot realize directional pair costs because its affinity is symmetric; the falsifiable threshold is total makespan < 244 (current) on the three-workload evaluation, driven by seeds whose true oracle cost at construction time is already below the incumbent's best seeds.

strategies.title: [LNS block-reinsertion with true-oracle arbitration] large neighborhood ruin of
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: conflict-block LNS (large-neighborhood ruin on the conflict graph)
Replacement scope: Replace the ILS tail's ruin-and-recreate perturbation (the random segment extraction/reinsertion in the final while-loop) with conflict-block ruin; keep `one_pass`/`local_search` and the construction stages as-is.
Compute budget: Each LNS iteration = one block removal (O(k)) + one greedy reinsertion (O(k·n) oracle calls, k≤8) + one `local_search` polish; cap k at 8 and reinsertion candidate slots at 10 per element; runs until the existing 85s deadline. Expected effect: fewer but far higher-yield perturbations than the current random segment moves.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent's perturbation removes a *contiguous random segment*, but contiguity in the current permutation is not where the cost lives — conflicts are keyed by shared data items. The new degree of freedom is removing a *conflict-connected block*: pick a random transaction, take its k strongest conflict neighbors (from the affinity matrix already computed), remove those k positions wherever they sit in the permutation, and reinsert them greedily one-by-one at the position (among 10 sampled slots) minimizing true oracle cost. This relocates an entire interacting subsystem coherently, which random segment moves and or-opt single reinsertions cannot reach because they only move contiguous or single elements.
Plan: (1) Reuse the existing `aff` matrix (already computed when parsing succeeds; fall back to random segment moves if `keys is None`). (2) Maintain the incumbent `cur_seq`; each LNS round: seed = random txn; block = its top-(k−1) affinity neighbors; remove those IDs from `cur_seq`; reinsert each greedily at the best of 10 sampled slots by `seq_cost`, accepting only full-permutation candidates. (3) Polish with existing `local_search`; accept-only-if-better, update global best. Validity: removal+reinsertion of distinct IDs preserves permutation; incumbent best is never discarded. Expected-gain check: the incumbent's escape moves are contiguous/random and cannot jointly relocate a scattered conflict clique; falsifiable threshold: total makespan < 244 with the same construction stage, measured on the three-workload evaluator.

strategies.title: [position-pair exchange ILS] exhaustive non-adjacent swap sweep as new neighborh
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: full swap-neighborhood sweep (all-pairs exchange local search)
Replacement scope: Replace the adjacent-swap stage inside `one_pass` (and complement the or-opt stage) with a full all-pairs exchange sweep; keep beam construction and everything else.
Compute budget: One sweep = O(n²) oracle calls (~10⁴ for n=100, each a cached tuple lookup); at most 2 sweeps per `one_pass` call, bounded by the existing per-workload deadline. Expected effect: a few seconds of extra oracle calls per workload, well within 85s.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent's swap neighborhood is adjacent-only, so moving a transaction across a long distance requires many sequential adjacent improvements, each of which must individually lower cost — a classic local-optimum trap. The new degree of freedom is the full transposition neighborhood: swapping any two positions i<j directly, taking the first improvement found (first-improvement over pairs ordered by distance band: try long-range swaps first since adjacent swaps are already covered). This reaches orderings the or-opt reinsertion misses too, because a swap is two simultaneous reinsertions that preserve relative order of everything else.
Plan: (1) In `one_pass`, after or-opt, iterate distance d from n−1 down to 1; for each i, try swapping seq[i], seq[i+d], evaluate `seq_cost`, return on first improvement. (2) Keep the existing segment-reversal and adjacent-swap stages after it as cheap fallbacks. (3) `local_search` loop unchanged (repeat until no improvement or deadline). Validity: swaps preserve permutation membership; the identity fallback and accept-only-if-better guard are untouched. Expected-gain check: the incumbent cannot realize a single-step long-range exchange (it needs a chain of individually-improving adjacent swaps); falsifiable threshold: total makespan < 244 on the evaluator, with the gain attributable to long-distance (d>4) swaps that the incumbent's neighborhoods never test in one move.

strategies.title: [key-centric insertion construction] conflict-key greedy insertion with true-ora
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: key-centric insertion construction
Replacement scope: Replace the directed-pair-order seeded construction block (the `D`/`dcost` greedy-append loop) inside `get_best_schedule`; keep the beam, ILS tail, cache, and deadlines intact.
Compute budget: Reuse the existing 10s construct deadline and 85s per-workload deadline; no new optimizer starts beyond the existing 3 randomized restarts. Evaluation-time effect neutral.
Gain mechanism: The current construction scores an appended transaction by summing *absolute* pair costs against all placed transactions, which is dominated by cheap transactions regardless of conflict order. The new degree of freedom is per-key arbitration: for each data key, collect the set of transactions touching it; use the true oracle on 2-element orderings only for transactions sharing a key, and build the seed by inserting each transaction into the position that minimizes oracle cost of the *prefix up to that point* (cheapest-insertion, as in TSP construction). This directly optimizes the actual makespan signal the incumbent's aggregate sum swamps.
Plan: (1) Parse keys as the incumbent already does (`parse_txn`); build key → list of txn indices. (2) Order transactions for insertion by descending number of conflicted keys (ties broken by oracle cost of the singleton). (3) Insert each transaction t by trying every position in the current partial sequence and evaluating `seq_cost(partial with t inserted)` — cached; accept the cheapest. This is O(n²) oracle calls, all cached and bounded by the construct deadline with a time check per insertion. (3 restarts with shuffled insertion order, as now.) (4) Pool completed seeds into the existing ILS tail exactly as constructed seeds are today. Validity: every seed is a full permutation built by insertion of all n distinct transactions; incumbent identity permutation remains the fallback before any search; only the EVOLVE block changes.
Expected-gain check: The new degree of freedom is position-aware cheapest-insertion scored by the true oracle (the incumbent's greedy append can only place t at the end); if any workload's optimum requires a conflicted transaction mid-sequence, the incumbent construction cannot produce it, and the falsifiable threshold is total makespan strictly below 240 on the three-workload evaluator.

strategies.title: [topological-chain decomposition] longest-path layering on the conflict digraph
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: topological-chain decomposition
Replacement scope: Replace the beam-search construction phase (the partial-permutation beam loop) in `get_best_schedule`; retain seq_cost cache, directed-pair data, ILS refinement, and deadlines.
Compute budget: One deterministic construction pass plus 2 randomized restarts, all inside the existing 10s construct window; beam time (~5–10s currently) is freed and flows to the ILS tail. Per-workload 85s deadline unchanged.
Gain mechanism: The beam explores prefixes by cost but has no notion of dependency *direction*: a write-then-read chain forces ordering regardless of prefix cost, and beam diversity by last transaction cannot recover a forced chain once pruned. New degree of freedom: build a directed conflict graph where edge i→j exists iff the oracle says cost([i,j]) < cost([j,i]) *and* they share keys; compute a topological layering (longest-path depth from sources via DFS on the DAG portion, cycle-breaking by removing the weakest-affinity back edge). The seed is transactions sorted by (layer, then within-layer by descending out-affinity), which is a geometrically different deterministic seed from cost-ranked prefixes.
Plan: (1) Reuse the incumbent's parsed keys and directed pair costs D (already computed). (2) Build digraph edges for conflicting pairs with the cheaper direction; break cycles by deleting the back edge with smallest affinity until acyclic (Kahn's algorithm). (3) Layer = longest path length; within each layer sort by total affinity descending. Concatenate layers → full permutation, scored by the oracle, pooled as an ILS seed. (2 restarts: within-layer order shuffled). (4) Remove the beam loop entirely; its budget goes to ILS. Validity: layer concatenation is a permutation of range(n); identity fallback and accept-only-if-better guards unchanged; only the EVOLVE block changes.
Expected-gain check: The incumbent cannot express a forced dependency chain (it prunes by prefix cost, not direction); the falsifiable evaluator threshold is total three-workload makespan strictly below 240, with the mechanism testable by checking that the layer seed's oracle cost beats the beam's best completion on at least one workload.

strategies.title: [multi-seed ILS portfolio] parallel-restart simulated-annealing tail replacing a
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: multi-seed annealing ILS
Replacement scope: Replace the ILS tail (the `local_search`/perturbation loop and its accept-only-if-better rule) in `get_best_schedule`; keep construction, beam, cache, and the 85s deadline.
Compute budget: 4 restarts × the remaining ~70s tail budget (time-sliced round-robin, ~17s each), each restart capped by wall-clock checks inside `one_pass` exactly as now; no change to total evaluation time.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent's ILS accepts only strict improvements, so it is trapped in the basin of its first seed; the observed code-change evidence shows all recent gains came from construction, not refinement, indicating the refinement is the local bottleneck. New degree of freedom: annealed acceptance — accept a candidate with probability exp(-(c−cur)/T) where T decays geometrically from T0 = 1% of incumbent cost to 0.01% over the budget, allowing downhill moves that or-opt cannot traverse in one step. Round-robin across 4 independent chains seeded from (identity, best beam completion, best constructed seed, layer seed) preserves diversity.
Plan: (1) Keep `one_pass` neighborhoods unchanged (or-opt, segment reversal, adjacent swaps). (2) Replace the accept rule: after `local_search` plateaus, apply the ruin-and-recreate perturbation and accept per the annealing rule; T decays per accepted-step count. (3) Track the global best across all chains; return it. (4) Guard: every candidate is a full permutation by construction (segment move preserves elements); incumbent best is always retained. Only the EVOLVE block changes.
Expected-gain check: The incumbent's refinement cannot escape a local basin (strict-improvement acceptance), whereas annealed acceptance can traverse it; the falsifiable evaluator threshold is total makespan strictly below 240, and the mechanism is falsifiable per-workload by comparing the annealed tail's best cost against the incumbent tail run for the same fixed seed.

strategies.title: [regret-suffix completion] partial-prefix regret-driven rollout replacing beam s
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: regret-suffix rollout construction
Replacement scope: Replace the beam-search expansion phase (the `while beam` loop and its `max_per_last` selection logic) inside `get_best_schedule`; keep the cached `seq_cost`, the directed-pair construction, and the ILS tail unchanged.
Compute budget: Same 10s construction cap and 85s per-workload deadline. At each of n rollout depths, evaluate all remaining unplaced transactions with the true oracle on the extended prefix (≤ n² oracle calls per rollout, n≤~30 keeps this inside the cap), 2 rollouts total; check the clock each depth.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent's beam selects successors by raw prefix cost, which biases toward cheap short-horizon prefixes that later become expensive; the new degree of freedom is a regret rule: at each depth, for each candidate next-transaction t, compute the *best two* successor costs among remaining options and prefer the candidate whose best alternative is much worse (regret = second-best − best), i.e., prioritize decisions that are costly to postpone, a decision-theoretic signal the incumbent's myopic beam cannot express. Complete each rollout greedily by regret, score the full permutation with the oracle, and feed completions plus the directed-pair seeds into the existing ILS tail. Validity: every rollout step appends a distinct unplaced transaction from range(n), so the result is a full permutation; the identity fallback and ILS tail are preserved. Expected-gain check: the new regret-based branching order is a degree of freedom absent from the incumbent's greedy prefix-cost beam; the falsifiable threshold is any total makespan strictly below the incumbent's current raw total (combined_score 4149.38 corresponds to total ≈ 240), measured on the same three-workload evaluation.

strategies.title: [key-group interleaving] conflict-key cluster-block construction with oracle-pri
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: conflict-key cluster-block interleave
Replacement scope: Replace the directed-pair greedy construction block (the `for r in range(3)` seeding loop and its `dcost` accumulation) with a key-cluster block construction; beam search and ILS tail stay.
Compute budget: Reuse the 10s construct deadline; clustering is O(n·k) set operations, block ordering uses ≤ n oracle calls per block, total ≤ ~3n oracle calls — well inside the cap; ILS tail budget unchanged.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent prices only *pairwise* directed costs and greedily chains transactions, which cannot capture that several transactions touching the same hot key should be scheduled as a near-contiguous block to pay the conflict delay only once. strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: regret-suffix rollout construction
Replacement scope: Replace the beam-search expansion phase (the `while beam` loop and its `max_per_last` selection logic) inside `get_best_schedule`; keep the cached `seq_cost`, the directed-pair construction, and the ILS tail unchanged.
Compute budget: Same 10s construction cap and 85s per-workload deadline. At each of n rollout depths, evaluate all remaining unplaced transactions with the true oracle on the extended prefix (≤ n² oracle calls per rollout, n≤~30 keeps this inside the cap), 2 rollouts total; check the clock each depth.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent's beam selects successors by raw prefix cost, which biases toward cheap short-horizon prefixes that later become expensive; the new degree of freedom is a regret rule: at each depth, for each candidate next-transaction t, compute the *best two* successor costs among remaining options and prefer the candidate whose best alternative is much worse (regret = second-best − best), i.e., prioritize decisions that are costly to postpone, a decision-theoretic signal the incumbent's myopic beam cannot express. Complete each rollout greedily by regret, score the full permutation with the oracle, and feed completions plus the directed-pair seeds into the existing ILS tail. Validity: every rollout step appends a distinct unplaced transaction from range(n), so the result is a full permutation; the identity fallback and ILS tail are preserved. Expected-gain check: the new regret-based branching order is a degree of freedom absent from the incumbent's greedy prefix-cost beam; the falsifiable threshold is any total makespan strictly below the incumbent's current raw total (combined_score 4149.38 corresponds to total ≈ 240), measured on the same three-workload evaluation.
